Abstract
The convergence of blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and cloud computing is catalyzing a paradigm shift in devel­
oping secure, intelligent, and scalable digital infrastructures. This triad of technologies is increasingly utilized to improve 
performance, transparency, and trust in engineering-driven and socio-technical environments. This study systematically 
reviews the evolution, integration strategies, and applications of blockchain, AI, and cloud computing in digital eco­
systems. The analysis is based on 108 peer-reviewed studies spanning the years 2012 to 2025. A comprehensive lit­
erature analysis was conducted to identify trends, synergies, and sector-specific implementations of these systems. The 
review explores how their integration supports real-world engineering and operational use cases. Blockchain contributes 
to decentralized architectures, secure data exchange, and identity verification. AI supports adaptive behavior, autonomous 
decision-making, and predictive analytics. Cloud computing offers the scalable infrastructure necessary for deployment. 
Key challenges addressed include interoperability, latency, security trade-offs, and resource allocation. Use cases in digital 
finance, supply chain management, and industrial automation demonstrate the effectiveness of this integration in building 
resilient, ethically aligned, and high-performance infrastructures. The findings offer valuable insights and technical consid­
erations for engineers and architects seeking to design next-generation cyber-physical systems that are secure, intelligent, 
and socially responsive.

1  Introduction
Blockchain is a promising technology as it mitigates secu­
rity concerns, eliminates fraud, and enhances transparency 
[1]. Initially linked to Bitcoin and non-fungible tokens 
(NFTs) in the 2010s, blockchain has now evolved into a 
management solution for multinational organizations. It 
enhances transparency in supply chains, secures health­
care data, revolutionizes gaming, and reshapes concepts 
of data and ownership. Blockchain, also known as distrib­
uted ledger technology (DLT), enables the secure exchange 
of digital data and cryptocurrencies. [2] Transactions are 
authenticated by multiple network nodes, accepted, and 
stored as blocks across devices. Each new transaction is 
added to the chain, creating a historical record that reduces 
hacking threats. This secure data exchange, free from third-
party involvement, makes blockchain highly attractive [3]. 
Beyond money transfers, blockchain’s transparency and 
versatility support applications across various industries, 
including energy, logistics, and education. Prior works have 
examined the evolution and recent advances of blockchain 
[4].
The paper also reviews blockchain transaction formats 
and their integration with cloud computing [5], presenting 
applications [6] and challenges in this domain [7]. Unre­
solved issues remain, particularly regarding interoperabil­
ity and research directions. Since its inception in the early 
2000s, blockchain has been regarded as disruptive in coop­
eration, payment automation, market monitoring, and trans­
action recording [8, 9]. Its decentralized design removes the 
need for central authorities, as mining nodes verify cryp­
tographically hashed transactions, creating timestamped, 
immutable, and accessible records [10].
Artificial intelligence (AI), which enables machines to 
learn from data and make informed decisions, is also grow­
ing rapidly, with a projected market value of USD 13 tril­
lion by 2030 [11]. Despite numerous approaches, ensuring 
secure information in smart homes remains unresolved 
[7–9]. Blockchain offers promising solutions for preventing 
command-and-control attacks and securing device connec­
tivity. Consensus among nodes ensures permanent transac­
tion records, making unauthorized access difficult without 
compromising multiple hubs [12].
In recent years, decentralized AI has emerged through the 
merging of blockchain and AI. Blockchain enables decen­
tralized, intermediary-free data execution and storage [13], 
while AI provides analysis and decision-making capabilities 
[14]. Smart contracts further enhance secure data sharing 
[15]. This integration supports decentralized decision-mak­
ing, enhances trust, and enables collaborative participation 
in processes [16]. Applications include healthcare, where 
blockchain secures patient data and AI extracts insights, as 
seen in solutions like BurstIQ [17–19]. The integration also 
benefits finance by increasing transaction speed and trust, 
and extends to 6 G networks, smart cities, banking, and 
autonomous vehicles [20]. Blockchain ensures the validity 
of information, supporting the secure storage of AI inputs 
and outputs [21].
This study reviews the literature on the integration of 
blockchain and AI, highlighting the benefits, applications, 
and challenges associated with this emerging technology. 
It aims to provide researchers with a clear understanding 
of the field’s evolution, identify practical implications, and 
outline key challenges. The structure is as follows: Section 
2 describes the research methodology for screening and

1.2  Key Findings
A systematic literature study was conducted to analyze the 
integration of blockchain technology with AI. Literature 
from six digital libraries and academic search engines, par­
ticularly publications from February 2024 to the present, 
was examined. An initial search identified 2,277 potentially 
relevant articles, which underwent a stringent screening pro­
cess based on titles, abstracts, full texts, manual searches, 
and snowballing of references. After this assessment, 101 
primary studies (PSs) met the inclusion criteria for detailed 
analysis.

The review addresses several key areas:
1.	 The study examines the mechanics and decade-long 
development of blockchain technology, highlighting its 
applications across multiple domains.
2.	 Major impediments in blockchain implementation are 
identified, and pragmatic strategies for addressing these 
challenges are discussed to support sustainable growth.
3.	 The analysis examines the interaction between 
blockchain and transaction platforms, as well as

5.1.2  Inequality and Access

often hindered by economic and technical barriers, poten­

systems require significant computational resources, tech­
nical expertise, and financial investment, which may limit 
accessibility for marginalized communities and develop­
ing regions. AI models also demand substantial data and 
computing power, reinforcing the divide between techno­
logically advanced economies and those with limited infra­
structure. To mitigate these disparities, initiatives promoting 
open-source blockchain frameworks, decentralized AI mod­
els, and affordable cloud computing solutions should be pri­
oritized to ensure wider participation in the digital economy.
5.1  Limitations and Potential Drawbacks of

The desegregation of blockchain, AI, and cloud computing 
faces up numerous opportunities across contrastive sectors. 
However, beside these benefits come various challenges that 
must be conservatively considered. Key issues let in ethical 
concerns, security risks, regulatory challenges, and scal­
ability limitations, all of which impinge on the effectualness 
and creditworthy use of these technologies. One substantial 
gainsay is ethical pertains related to data privacy, algorith­
mic bias, and transparency. AI systems hinge on vast datasets 
to make decisions, and when commingled with blockchain’s 
immutable nature, consequences of data ownership and con­
sent become complex. Ensuring fairness in AI-driven deter­
minations is another concern, as predetermined training 
data can contribute to discriminatory outcomes. Addition­
ally, while blockchain enhances transparency, it may also 
debunk sensitive information that should remain confiden­
tial. Directing these ethical challenges requires the develop­
ment of privacy-preserving techniques, fairness-aware AI 
models, and responsible data-sharing policies.

The environmental impact of blockchain, particularly 
networks that rely on Proof of Work (PoW) consensus 
mechanisms, is a growing ethical concern. PoW-based 
blockchains, such as Bitcoin, consume vast amounts of 
electricity, contributing to carbon emissions and environ­
mental degradation. This energy-intensive process raises 
sustainability concerns, necessitating the exploration of 
alternative consensus models such as Proof of Stake (PoS), 
Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS), and hybrid blockchain 
architectures. Additionally, integrating AI-driven optimiza­
tion techniques can enhance energy efficiency in blockchain 
networks, reducing their ecological footprint while main­
taining security and functionality.
5.1.4  Accountability and Governance
Blockchain operates as a decentralized system, eliminat­
ing the need for intermediaries and centralized authorities. 
While this decentralization enhances trust and transparency, 
it also creates accountability challenges. In the absence of a 
central governing body, determining responsibility in cases 
of fraud, system failures, or unethical use becomes difficult. 
Additionally, AI algorithms deployed on blockchain sys­
tems may introduce biases or automated decision-making 
concerns without clear regulatory oversight. To address 
these governance issues, regulatory frameworks must 
evolve to include mechanisms for dispute resolution, ethi­
cal AI auditing, and legally enforceable smart contract poli­
cies. Hybrid governance models combining decentralized 
decision-making with regulatory compliance could help 
establish accountability while preserving the advantages of 
blockchain technology.

6  Discussion and Conclusions
Blockchain technology has rapidly evolved beyond its initial 
applications in the financial sector, demonstrating potential 
across a wide range of industries. Its core features—immu­
tability, transparency, decentralized architecture, and secure 
data management—make it a transformative tool for enhanc­
ing trust and accountability in digital ecosystems. However, 
despite its advantages, blockchain adoption faces several 
challenges, including high energy consumption, limited 
scalability, and complex infrastructure requirements.
The integration of blockchain with cloud computing has 
emerged as a promising solution to address these challenges. 
Cloud platforms provide scalable infrastructure, flexible 
resource allocation, and on-demand computational power, 
which can complement blockchain’s decentralized architec­
ture. This synergy facilitates the deployment of blockchain-
based applications while mitigating issues such as network 
congestion and high operational costs.
The present study systematically reviews research on 
blockchain–cloud integration, analyzing trends in health­
care, finance, smart cities, and other domains. It also 
explores the concept of Blockchain-as-a-Service (BaaS) and 
compares services offered by leading cloud service provid­
ers. Through this analysis, the study highlights both oppor­
tunities and challenges in the field, raising key questions for 
future research:
	
●
What technical and organizational challenges are asso­
ciated with blockchain–cloud integration?
	
●
Which domains stand to benefit most from BaaS adop­
tion in the near future?
	
●
How can pricing models and Service Level Agreements 
(SLAs) be structured to ensure efficiency and quality of 
service (QoS)?
	
●
What architectural frameworks are most suitable for 
implementing robust BaaS solutions?
By addressing these questions, researchers and practitioners 
can better understand the current state of blockchain–cloud 
integration and identify pathways for innovation.

6.2  Conclusion and Future Scope
The integration of blockchain and cloud computing rep­
resents a transformative frontier for both research and 
industrial applications. This study consolidates existing 
knowledge on blockchain–cloud integration while high­
lighting key challenges, opportunities, and trends. By 
addressing critical issues such as scalability, Quality of 
Service (QoS), infrastructure optimization, and secure ser­
vice deployment, blockchain–cloud ecosystems can achieve 
enhanced efficiency, transparency, and trustworthiness. 
These insights provide a roadmap for researchers, practitio­
ners, and policymakers to develop innovative solutions that 
leverage the strengths of both technologies, enabling more 
secure, intelligent, and decentralized digital infrastructures 
across domains including finance, healthcare, smart cities, 
and supply chain management.
The future scope of blockchain–cloud integration is vast 
and multifaceted. Research can focus on developing scal­
able and high-performance consensus mechanisms, design­
ing flexible Blockchain-as-a-Service (BaaS) frameworks 
with customizable SLAs, and exploring the convergence 
of AI and IoT with blockchain–cloud systems for real-time 
decision-making and intelligent automation. Further inves­
tigations can enhance smart contract design for secure, 
interoperable, and automated resource management, as 
well as strengthen data privacy and access control in cloud 
environments. Additionally, domain-specific applications 
in smart agriculture, healthcare, and decentralized finance 
(DeFi) hold significant potential. Attention to sustainable 
and energy-efficient blockchain solutions, along with novel 
architectural frameworks for decentralized urban systems 
and critical infrastructures, will further drive the adoption 
of blockchain–cloud technologies. Collectively, these direc­
tions promise to unlock the full potential of blockchain–
cloud integration, fostering resilient, secure, and intelligent 
digital ecosystems for the future [107, 108].

Abstract: The convergence of blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and cloud computing is catalyzing a paradigm shift in devel­ oping secure, intelligent, and scalable digital infrastructures. This triad of technologies is increasingly utilized to improve performance, transparency, and trust in engineering-driven and socio-technical environments. This study systematically reviews the evolution, integration strategies, and applications of blockchain, AI, and cloud computing in digital eco­ systems. The analysis is based on 108 peer-reviewed studies spanning the years 2012 to 2025. A comprehensive lit­ erature analysis was conducted to identify trends, synergies, and sector-specific implementations of these systems. The review explores how their integration supports real-world engineering and operational use cases. Blockchain contributes to decentralized architectures, secure data exchange, and identity verification. AI supports adaptive behavior, autonomous decision-making, and predictive analytics. Cloud computing offers the scalable infrastructure necessary for deployment. Key challenges addressed include interoperability, latency, security trade-offs, and resource allocation. Use cases in digital finance, supply chain management, and industrial automation demonstrate the effectiveness of this integration in building resilient, ethically aligned, and high-performance infrastructures. The findings offer valuable insights and technical consid­ erations for engineers and architects seeking to design next-generation cyber-physical systems that are secure, intelligent, and socially responsive. Highlights ● This article accentuates the extensive use of blockchain, cloud computing, and AI principles, emphasizing their crucial significance in the contemporary digital environment and paths in which blockchain technology may be employed to automate financial transactions, enhance the security of personal data and records, facilitate cross-border transactions, verify identities, execute smart contracts, utilize cryptocurrencies, and manage supply chains. ● This research systematically assesses the development and practical application of blockchain, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence technologies over the past decade. This study primarily focuses on monitoring the progress, practi­ cal applications, and benefits of blockchain technology in the context of financial transactions. ● This article probes the symbiotic relationship between artificial intelligence, cloud and blockchain technology, analyzing the evolution and fundamental concepts of their integration from 2012 to 2025. This paper also presents a detailed analy­ sis of 108 research works acquitted over the past decade. The study provides a comprehensive examination of the current state and fundamental principles related to the integration of artificial intelligence, cloud, and blockchain technology. ● This paper offers a comprehensive analysis of the major obstacles confronted by blockchain technology, examin­ ing its wide-ranging applications over several industries and its socko role in transaction systems and the domain of cryptocurrencies.
